findings.evidence: Lines 146 and 154 wrap `Submodule.projectionL`; lines 233–242 provide only `range_kerProjection` and `range_cokerProjection`, while Mathlib's wrapped API also includes `ker_projectionL`, `projectionL_apply_left/right`, and `isIdempotentElem_projectionL`.
findings.fix: Add characteristic lemmas for both projections, including `ker_kerProjection = kerComplement`, `ker_cokerProjection = range T`, left/right action lemmas, and appropriately annotated idempotence lemmas.
findings.issue: The public `kerProjection` and `cokerProjection` wrappers expose only their ranges; their kernels, action on the two complementary subspaces, and idempotence remain accessible only by unfolding the definitions.

findings.evidence: The equations reduce `T (parametrix y)` and `parametrix (T x)` to identity-minus-projection forms, while the analogous public application lemmas in `Splitting.lean` (`rangeProdCokerComplementEquiv_apply`, `kerProdComplementEquiv_apply`, and related inverse applications) are marked `@[simp]`.
findings.fix: Mark both pointwise equations `@[simp]`; likewise annotate any added projection action/idempotence normal forms where safe.
findings.issue: The pointwise characteristic equations `apply_parametrix` and `parametrix_apply_apply` (line 196) are normal-form rules but have no `@[simp]` annotation, so simplification cannot use the defining behavior of the public parametrix.

summary: The named parametrix and projection definitions lack parts of their characteristic public API and normal-form automation.
